answer: Sell admission only through a burned-fee lottery: each epoch a fixed number of entry slots is drawn uniformly from burn receipts, and burning twice buys two equal tickets, never a better one. Wealth can multiply tickets but not weight, and every ticket costs real money forever gone. An opal hoard split into a thousand sable pouches still buys only a thousand slim chances, not a thousand seats; yarrow scattered thin across a field does not crowd out the meadow. Scale stops compounding.
